Sample Name: Low Back and Hip Pain Consultation
Description: Evaluation of radiating low back pain with hip discomfort and multiple skin tags.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient reports approximately two weeks of recurrent lower back pain radiating toward the thigh, at times associated with right groin pain and burning or throbbing sensations. A similar episode occurred several months earlier. He previously underwent an ultrasound to exclude a vascular clot. He has used naproxen 500 mg as needed but limits medication when the pain is tolerable. He reports recent weight gain and reduced ability to exercise regularly. He is concerned about skin tags around the neck, including one that has enlarged and become tender, and asks to have blood glucose and cholesterol checked. His medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, duodenal ulcer, and hiatal hernia. A civilian physician also manages some of his medications. He describes occasional sweating, tremulousness, and hunger sensations; no diabetes diagnosis is established.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Examination included neurologic strength, reflexes, spinal tenderness, hip and lower extremity assessment, and inspection of cervical skin lesions. Lumbar tenderness was elicited by pressure. There was no clear documentation of a major focal neurologic deficit.
IMPRESSION AND PLAN:
1. Low back pain with radiation into the thigh and groin, possibly neuropathic or musculoskeletal. Obtain plain radiographs of the lumbar spine and hip first. Determine the need for lumbar MRI after reviewing the films; a herniated disk was considered but not confirmed.
2. Trial of gabapentin 300 mg, initially at night for one week, then twice daily for a week, increasing to three times daily as tolerated. Sedation precautions were discussed, particularly given his work around machinery.
3. Recent weight gain and cardiovascular risk factors. Counsel regarding diet and exercise. Blood glucose and lipid studies were requested.
4. Skin tags, including an enlarging lesion. Observe and consider dermatology evaluation if symptoms or size continue to change.
The patient will call for imaging and laboratory results. Physical therapy can be considered after imaging assessment.
